newsitem.title: USA: US Sen has bill to change newspaper ownership law.
newsitem.headline: US Sen has bill to change newspaper ownership law.

text.p: An influential U.S. senator Thursday introduced legislation that would eliminate a decades-old law that bars companies from owning a newspaper along with a television or radio station in the same town.
"This legislation would remove one of the most archaic provisions remaining in telecommunications law," said Sen John McCain, an Arizona Republican who heads the commerce committee.
"It is not surprising that, in this era of media diversity, newspapers have found it tough going, their numbers steadily declining over the years," McCain added in a statement.

The newspaper/broadcast cross-ownership prohibition was enacted because of fears that common control of both types of media outlets in the same market could result in the public's getting only one point of view on important issues.
The Federal Communications Commission has the power to waive the rules and allow a company to own both a newspaper and a local radio or TV station.
Media mogul Rupert Murdoch received such clearance for his ownership of the New York Post and the TV station in New York owned by the Fox network.
McCain argued that the number of outlets for news, information and entertainment has grown dramatically, negating the need for any restrictions.
He said that many radio and TV stations are now supplemented by multichannel news and entertainment outlets like cable and satellite TV.
"Diversity of viewpoints is as close as clicking on the Internet," McCain said. "It's time to finally get rid of this relic."
